transcript.content: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, thank you. Well, what really brought me in is that... I've been having this issue where my wife will be telling me about things, like my cousin’s appointments or rides. And I’m looking right at her while she's talking, but a minute later I realize I didn’t actually take in half of what she said. It's been happening enough that I figured I should probably get it checked out.
How long have you been noticing this difficulty taking in what people are saying to you?
Well, I'd say it's been noticeably harder for about 11 months now. That was right around the time my cousin moved in with us after having surgery.
Did you experience similar difficulties with attention or staying focused when you were a child in school?

Yeah, I did. Even way back in grade school—definitely before I was 12—my teachers used to tell my parents that I was a bright kid, but I was just always daydreaming. I'd, you know, leave my finished homework sitting right inside my desk, and they were always having to remind me to actually finish my classwork. So... yeah, I guess it's been an issue for a long time.
Do you often feel restless on the inside, or find yourself constantly fidgeting and having trouble sitting still?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. I don't have any trouble sitting still, and I wouldn't say I feel restless on the inside. It's really just my mind wandering off, not my body needing to move around.
